subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should maintainers accept for the native-Linux VPS reasoning-latency investigation: a docs/runbook synthesis of existing signals, new instrumentation work, or both?
rationale: The issue is valid and aligned with performance priorities, but the remaining work is an analysis/product scoping decision rather than a single reproducible code defect.

options.title: Scope a performance runbook
options.body: Document a repeatable native-Linux measurement plan first, using existing diagnostics and identifying only measured instrumentation gaps for later PRs.

options.title: Sponsor instrumentation first
options.body: Prioritize missing spans around the largest suspected prep/runtime layers before writing a public analysis guide.

options.title: Close as support-only
options.body: Treat the specific CPX32 setup as out-of-repo support unless a reporter or maintainer can provide fresh trace data.

recommendation.title: Scope a performance runbook
recommendation.body: Document a repeatable native-Linux measurement plan first, using existing diagnostics and identifying only measured instrumentation gaps for later PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-history owner across the docs, context, memory, Telegram, and embedded-runner diagnostics surfaces that would define the runbook scope.
